phase: Phase G - Crop Sequence Compatibility Rules
notes: Rules govern consecutive transitions (predecessor -> successor) and rolling multi-year return windows using Phase E ITGC / ICARDA / FAO pathology evidence.

sequence_rules.name: Annual-Perennial Scope Separation
sequence_rules.rule: Never include perennial tree crop OLIVE inside an annual crop sequence slot or convert olive groves into annual cereal rotations.

sequence_rules.name: Cereal Monoculture & Grass-Weed Guard
sequence_rules.source: CON_11_SEQUENCE; ITGC / ICARDA Algeria cereal pathology
sequence_rules.rule: Same-species consecutive wheat (Durum->Durum / Soft->Soft) or cereal->cereal triggers WARNING at 2 consecutive cereal campaigns (take-all, Fusarium, wild oat buildup) and HARD FAIL if >=3 consecutive cereal campaigns occur without a broadleaf/forage/fallow break.

sequence_rules.name: Solanaceae 3-4 Year Return Break
sequence_rules.source: CON_11_SEQUENCE; DSA Guelma / Cahiers Agricultures Bouchegouf studies
sequence_rules.rule: Never plant Tomato after Tomato, Potato after Potato, Tomato after Potato, or Potato after Tomato within a 3-year return gap (Verticillium/Fusarium wilt, nematodes, late blight, Orobanche).

sequence_rules.name: Food Legume Return Interval & Orobanche / Ascochyta Guard
sequence_rules.source: CON_11_SEQUENCE; ITGC/MDPI & ICARDA-ITGC Winter Chickpea Program
sequence_rules.rule: Consecutive or <3 yr same food legume or Faba Bean <-> Lentil fails immediately (HARD_CONSTRAINT: Orobanche crenata, Ascochyta spp., Botrytis, Fusarium). Different legume genera within <3 yr (e.g. Faba Bean -> Wheat -> Winter Chickpea, gap=2 yr) trigger SOFT WARNING for shared Sclerotinia/Fusarium and secondary Orobanche carryover because crop_profiles specify >=3 yr within chickpea/faba species while Ascochyta is genus-specific.

sequence_rules.name: Sunflower Sclerotinia & Orobanche cumana Break
sequence_rules.rule: Consecutive or <3 yr repeated Sunflower fails immediately due to Sclerotinia rot and Orobanche cumana buildup.

sequence_rules.name: Vetch-Oat Fallow Replacement & Oat Host Caution
sequence_rules.rule: Single Vetch-Oat inside Cereal -> Vetch-Oat -> Cereal is an approved fallow-replacement break if hay is cut in Apr-May before grass-weed seed shed (PASS). Consecutive Vetch-Oat -> Vetch-Oat or frequent 2-year return around cereal (Vetch-Oat -> Cereal -> Vetch-Oat) triggers WARNING for recurring Avena grass-weed/host pressure, mandatory early hay cut timing, and shoot-N/biomass export if baled off-field.

sequence_rules.name: Legume -> Cereal Break & Symbiotic N Advantage
sequence_rules.rule: Food legume or Vetch-Oat followed by Durum Wheat / Soft Wheat / Barley interrupts cereal root diseases/wild oats and supplies organic N/residue synergy (conditioned on valid pulse gap & adequate moisture).

sequence_rules.name: Soil Cover & Consecutive Bare Fallow Prevention
sequence_rules.rule: Consecutive Bare Fallow -> Bare Fallow fails (zero productivity & soil cover loss); single Bare Fallow on low-SOC (<18 g/kg) or unmeasured-slope soils triggers WARNING favoring Vetch-Oat replacement.

sequence_rules.name: Subsoil Moisture Depletion & Harvest-Planting Overlap
sequence_rules.rule: Deep-rooted Sunflower before rainfed Winter Cereal warns of deep profile moisture depletion if Autumn rains arrive late; Autumn Potato (Nov-Dec harvest) into Winter Cereal/Pulse warns of severe field harvest-planting calendar overlap.

sequence_rules.name: Missing Crop History Uncertainty Guard
sequence_rules.rule: When prior crop history before seq[0] is null ('NOT_PROVIDED') or empty ('EXPLICITLY_CONFIRMED_EMPTY') or resolves to crop_id_resolved=null, pathogen break intervals for seq[0] are evaluated as UNKNOWN rather than assumed safe.
